clue.text: Attendant for better publisher stops person shouting

indicators.note: to stop something up is to plug it, so one piece sits plugged inside another

blocks.note: a town crier is a person who shouts out news
Oxford University Press, a publisher

explanation.surface: An assistant at a publishing house tries to silence a loud colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' here is one who bets, not a comparative; OUP is the standard abbreviation for Oxford University Press.
explanation.definitionFit: The casino employee who runs a gaming table and pays out or collects stakes attends to the gamblers placing wagers.

clue.text: Composed lyrical melody? Not all of it

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is used, so the letters are found within it rather than taken whole

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A songwriter's tune sounds tranquil, but only in parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composed' looks like it is about writing music, matching 'melody', but it means self-possessed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone composed is serene and unflustered, keeping their emotions under control.

clue.text: Felon ultimately with not a single regret turned up in cell

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the word is kept
in a down clue, turning something up makes it read from bottom to top, backwards

blocks.note: the last letter of felon
not a single one means none, NO
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: A remorseless criminal surfaces in a prison cell.
explanation.walkthrough: The prison 'cell' of the surface is a biological one; only NO plus RUE flips, the N stays at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A nerve cell that transmits electrical impulses is a specific type of cell in the body.

clue.text: A supplier of iron, this person blocks trade supply

indicators.note: supply here is the adverb of supple, meaning flexibly, so the letters bend into a new order
to block a passage is to sit in the middle of it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: the five letters rearranged
the setter referring to themself

explanation.surface: An iron merchant finds someone obstructing the supply chain of their business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like a noun meaning provision, but it is read as the adverb from supple, meaning flexibly.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef and lamb are rich dietary sources of the mineral, so the food provides nutritional iron.

clue.text: Eccentric coerced us to install old form of program

indicators.note: installing puts something inside a system, so a letter is placed among the others
eccentric means off-centre and odd, so the letters are thrown into a strange order

blocks.note: taken as written
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An odd character pressured the staff into installing an outdated version of some software.
explanation.walkthrough: The O goes in among the letters of COERCED US before they are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: Programmers write human-readable instructions that are later compiled; that text is one way a program exists.

clue.text: Drink drop of Bourbon, in the mood for it

indicators.note: a drop is the smallest amount, so just the first letter is taken

blocks.note: the first letter of Bourbon
randy means sexually eager; 'it' is slang for sex

explanation.surface: Someone fancies a splash of American whiskey and is in the right frame of mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' as a euphemism for sex turns the innocent phrase into RANDY; Bourbon here only lends its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Distilled from wine, this spirit is an alcoholic beverage, so it counts as a drink.

clue.text: Need ground by minor thoroughfare extended

indicators.note: something ground is crushed and broken up, so its letters are reformed

blocks.note: a B-road is a minor road in Britain
the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Land is required next to a country lane that has been lengthened.
explanation.walkthrough: British roads are graded A (main) and B (minor), so a minor thoroughfare is a B ROAD; the anagram follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: To widen or enlarge something is to stretch its scope, a synonym of made wider.

clue.text: Where one may serve royal assembly

blocks.note: first meaning: a tennis or squash playing area
second meaning: a monarch's household and courtiers

explanation.walkthrough: 'Serve' suggests attending a monarch, which fits the second meaning; it is actually the tennis serve.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis players serve on a marked playing surface, and a sovereign's retinue gathered together shares the same name.

clue.text: Divine female thus entertained by Carmen?

indicators.note: a host entertains a guest in their home, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: the Automobile Association, a British motoring organisation of car men
then can mean therefore, thus

explanation.surface: An opera singer playing Carmen hosts a goddess-like woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Carmen suggests Bizet's opera heroine; split as car men it is the AA, the UK breakdown-recovery association, flagged by the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the Greek goddess of wisdom, so a deity who is a woman.

clue.text: Sea creature, maybe otter, crossing lake with parent

indicators.note: to cross something is to span it, so the outer piece stretches around the others

blocks.note: otter is one kind of fur, used for pelts
L is the standard abbreviation for lake
an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: An otter swims across a lake with its mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sea creature, maybe otter' reads as one phrase, but the otter belongs to the wordplay as an example of a fur.
explanation.definitionFit: A grey-and-white seabird related to petrels spends its life over the ocean, so it is a marine animal.

clue.text: Mathematician, following degree, is developing

indicators.note: one thing following another comes after it, which fixes the order of the two parts

blocks.note: a Master of Arts degree
Alan Turing, the British mathematician

explanation.surface: A mathematician who has just earned a degree is growing as a scholar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' tells you the mathematician comes after the degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Growing up or ripening over time means progressing towards full adulthood, a synonym of developing.

clue.text: Hotel by peninsula bordering Northern Ireland

indicators.note: a border runs round the edge, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the Iberian Peninsula of Spain and Portugal
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: A hotel sits on a peninsula near the border of Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Northern Ireland' is a false unit: Northern gives N and Ireland is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the Latin name the Romans used for the island west of Britain, now poetic.

clue.text: Part of ship's mooring - need to cast off back at sea

indicators.note: casting off the back drops the final letter
at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
the word without its final letter

explanation.surface: A sailor needs to cast off a boat's mooring rope from the back and head out to sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast off' is nautical in the surface, but here it removes the last letter of need; the 's stands for has.
explanation.definitionFit: The compartment housing a vessel's propulsion machinery is one section below deck.

clue.text: Record producer John still entertains largely just using covers

indicators.note: covers are the outside of something, so only the outer letters are kept
to entertain a guest is to take them in, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: even can mean still, as in even better
the first and last letters, with the inner ARGEL thrown away

explanation.surface: A music producer still mostly works with cover versions.
explanation.walkthrough: John Evelyn was the 17th-century English diarist; a diarist produces a record, not an album.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous English diarist kept a written record of his times, making him a producer of records.

clue.text: Warship in fix, beset by doom

indicators.note: to be beset is to be surrounded on all sides, so one piece is enclosed

blocks.note: fate and doom are synonyms
to rig is to fix a result dishonestly

explanation.surface: A battleship in a tight spot is surrounded by impending disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In fix' suggests being in trouble, but fix is a verb meaning to rig.
explanation.definitionFit: A medium-sized naval escort vessel is a fighting ship used by navies.

clue.text: What's seen twice in Tate: outstanding drawing

blocks.note: the only letter that appears twice in the word
a debt outstanding is still owing

explanation.surface: A superb drawing hangs at the Tate gallery and is viewed twice.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a London art gallery, which points 'outstanding drawing' towards art; drawing means pulling, as a tow truck does.
explanation.definitionFit: Hauling a vehicle behind another means pulling it along, one sense of drawing.

clue.text: Medicinal powder left over in kind of cigarette

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it

blocks.note: Camel is a cigarette brand
L is the abbreviation for left
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Some medicinal powder remains, tucked into a hand-rolled cigarette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left over' reads as remaining but splits into two abbreviations, L and O.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercurous chloride was formerly given as a purgative drug in white powdered form.

clue.text: You once also bitten by the barking canine

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so the letters go wild
something bitten is gripped between jaws, so it sits inside

blocks.note: an archaic form of you
too means also
the three letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone was bitten by a yapping dog in the past, and so was the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canine' and 'barking' paint a dog, but the canine is a tooth and barking means crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: An upper pointed tooth beneath the eye is the same as a canine tooth.

clue.text: Last capital of County Down

indicators.note: a capital letter is the initial one, so the first letter is taken

blocks.note: the first letter of County
a team down is behind in the score

explanation.surface: The final county town of County Down in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: County Down is a real Northern Irish county, so the phrase reads as a unit; it splits into C and a word for down.
explanation.definitionFit: The final remarks of a speech are its closing ones, so the adjective means final.

clue.text: Poet's previously gained and regularly earned returns

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept
something that returns comes back the way it went, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: to win is to gain
the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A poet's past work gained and steadily earned good financial returns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poet's' marks the word as archaic, the kind found in old verse.
explanation.definitionFit: An old literary word meaning before this time, used in verse for formerly.

clue.text: Game show, one for Irishman

blocks.note: RU is rugby union
to air something is to show or broadcast it
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A television game show has a spot for one contestant from Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game show' is a false unit: the game and the show are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a traditional Gaelic given name for boys, so it names a man from Ireland.

clue.text: Needless struggles abated

indicators.note: something that struggles thrashes about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Pointless fighting has died down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Struggles' looks like the subject of the sentence but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: When a storm or pain eases it diminishes in strength, which is a synonym of reduced.

clue.text: Team audibly expressed exasperation

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so a word is replaced by one pronounced the same

blocks.note: a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: A sports team loudly vented their frustration.
explanation.walkthrough: The team supplies a word whose pronunciation matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Letting out a long deep breath is a common way of showing weary frustration.

clue.text: Relative aboard sizable vessels? They drift around

indicators.note: a passenger aboard is carried inside a vessel, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: vats are large tanks or containers
a grandmother

explanation.surface: A family member on board big ships watches boats drifting past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessels' suggests ships, which fits 'aboard' and 'drift', but these vessels are containers.
explanation.definitionFit: Homeless wanderers with no fixed abode roam from place to place without settling.

clue.text: Protest and say, with outline of scowl, "I'm in pain!"

indicators.note: an outline traces only the edge, so the outer letters are kept

blocks.note: in casual speech, 'she goes' means 'she says'
the first and last letters
an exclamation of pain

explanation.surface: A protester frowns and complains of being hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: The informal go for say is the step most solvers miss.
explanation.definitionFit: British industrial action where workers deliberately work slowly is a form of workplace protest short of a strike.

clue.text: Garment in this fashion has designer label

blocks.note: so means in this way
the Calvin Klein fashion label

explanation.surface: A piece of clothing in the current style carries a big-name brand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' belongs to 'in this fashion', meaning so, not to the clothing theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Footwear worn under shoes is an item of clothing, so it counts as one.

clue.text: Men, currently popular, hosting ball for stars

indicators.note: a host has guests inside their home, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: OR is Other Ranks, soldiers who are not officers
what is in is fashionable now
a ball is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: Fashionable men throw a party for celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars' suggests celebrities at a ball, but it means a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hunter is a prominent constellation, a named group of stars in the night sky.

clue.text: Urban area that each other across answer has here

blocks.note: surface reading: a district of a town

blocks.clueFragment: that each other across answer has here
blocks.note: setter's reading: the other across answers each conceal a place name inside them

explanation.walkthrough: This is the puzzle's theme: across answers hide cities within, such as TURIN inside MATURING, OSLO inside GOSLOW and BERN inside HIBERNIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The deprived central district of a large town is a kind of urban area, and each hidden place is a town inside a word.
